questions.prompt: A colleague is your close friend. In front of a client you call them “babe” and tease them by first name only. What did you confuse?
options: Warmth with the Zura standard. Familiarity does not remove professionalism, and friendship does not permit disrespect.
Leadership with friendship, so titles never apply.

questions.prompt: You need to tell another therapist that Client Sam is waiting. Which line matches the internal standard?
You say “Yes, Sir” with sarcastic volume and a dismissive face. Why is this still a failure?
options: The word is enough; tone is private.
A respectful title spoken disrespectfully is still disrespect. The word must match the tone.
Sarcasm is allowed if the title is correct.

questions.prompt: A Lead Therapist holds the LT role today. You want to make responsibilities clear without creating fear. What is appropriate?
options: “The LT will assess the routine.” or “LT Stacey” where helpful.
Never use roles; roles create superiority.

questions.prompt: You do not know the client's name and keep saying “that woman.” What should you do?
options: Keep describing appearance so you never ask.
Politely ask: “Please Sir/Ma, may I have your name?” then use it appropriately.

questions.prompt: You need to correct a junior therapist's wording in public, in a humiliating tone. What is the standard?
options: Correction should not become humiliation. Respect remains even when correcting.
Leaders may belittle because leadership permits it.

questions.prompt: You speak extra sweetly to a wealthy-looking client and casually to another. What did the article forbid?
options: Using Sir and Ma at all.
Speaking differently to someone simply because they appear wealthy, influential or important.

questions.prompt: In a handover you say, “Thr. Jane, Client Michael reported pain around his shoulder.” Why is this stronger than “Jane, the guy has shoulder issues”?
options: It is excessive formality for its own sake.
It maintains professional identity, names the client as a client, and keeps the handover clear.
Work names should never be used.

questions.prompt: A therapist repeatedly mocks leaders with titles used as jokes. How does the article classify this?
options: Repeated mocking of colleagues or leaders is a professional conduct concern.
Only a problem if a client complains in writing.

questions.prompt: The client prefers a known title. You ignore it and use a different one because it is “more formal.” What should you do?
options: Where the client's preferred title is known, that preference should be respected.
Only use first names with clients.

title: SECTION B — FILL IN THE GAP

questions.prompt: Complete: “At Zura Spa, familiarity does not remove professionalism, friendship does not permit disrespect, and leadership does not permit anyone to _____."
Complete the Mode-of-Address Standard: “IDENTIFY → ADDRESS → RESPECT → _____."
Complete: “THE WORD MUST MATCH THE _____. A respectful title spoken disrespectfully is still disrespect."
Complete: “The purpose is not excessive formality. It is to maintain a clear _____."
Complete: “We can be warm without becoming careless, familiar without becoming disrespectful, friendly without becoming inappropriate, and firm without becoming _____."
When referring to a client within the team, the article prefers Client + Name over which kind of language?
options: “That man,” “the guy inside,” “that customer,” or identifying people by appearance or nationality.
“Mr. Samuel” when speaking to the client.

questions.prompt: Approved direct-address forms for clients include…
options: Babe, guy, and first name only.
Mr. + Name, Ms. + Name, Sir, Ma, and Madam.

questions.prompt: The hospital comparison in the article is used to explain that…
options: just as a hospital consistently refers to the person receiving care as a patient, we consistently recognize the person receiving our service as a client.

questions.prompt: In the Quick Guide, how is a Therapist Guide addressed?
options: TG / TG Jane (example: TG Mabel in the role section)

questions.prompt: The closing standard says every person receiving our service remains…
options: a client: Client Sam. Client Grace.
